answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock 100 copper tokens for 30 days before bidding for work. At each vertex of its trading graph, the same bond rule applies, whether an account uses a raven avatar or a company logo. Creating names is cheap, but running 1,000 eligible identities ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing a capital cost that grows with the swarm. This limits cheap sybils, though wealthy attackers can still pay.
